implementation_constraints: reads one JSON value from stdin, prints one line, exits 0

unresolved_intent.decision: reject bool as a valid age even though bool is a subclass of int in Python
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec says age must be an integer; a JSON true/false is not an integer value and admitting Python's bool-as-int subclassing would silently accept malformed input

unresolved_intent.decision: any JSON value that parses successfully but is not a list (e.g. an object, number, or string) is treated identically to a JSON parse failure and yields ERROR
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec only requires the top-level value to be a JSON array; it does not distinguish parse failures from valid-but-wrong-shape JSON, so both collapse to the same ERROR path

unresolved_intent.decision: records with extra fields beyond first/last/age are accepted and the extra fields are silently ignored
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec's out-of-scope section states no other fields are read or preserved, implying presence of extras is not itself an error condition

unresolved_intent.decision: empty or whitespace-only stdin fails json.loads and is treated as malformed input, producing ERROR
unresolved_intent.rationale: an empty input is not a valid JSON array literal, so it falls under the general malformed-input rule rather than being special-cased as an empty array

unresolved_intent.decision: use json.dumps default compact-ish formatting (no indent, default separators) since key order/whitespace is explicitly unconstrained
unresolved_intent.rationale: AC-TR-06 states only structure and values are fixed, so no extra effort is spent matching a particular formatting style

compilation_report.constraint_handling: r2: second blind run of the same model on the same canonical package (ADR-027 intra-model variance)
